english: For a real number $t>0$, let $V(t)$ denote the variance of the four observations $t,\ 2t,\ \dfrac{576}{t},\ \dfrac{1152}{t}$. Then the minimum value of $V(t)$ over all $t>0$ is ______.
hindi: वास्तविक संख्या $t>0$ के लिए माना $V(t)$ चार प्रेक्षणों $t,\ 2t,\ \dfrac{576}{t},\ \dfrac{1152}{t}$ का प्रसरण है। तब सभी $t>0$ पर $V(t)$ का न्यूनतम मान ______ है।
solution_full: The observations are $t,\ \dfrac{576}{t}$ and twice each of these. Let $s=t+\dfrac{576}{t}>0$.
$V$ increases with $s$ for $s>0$, so $V$ is least when $s$ is least.
By AM-GM, $t+\dfrac{576}{t}\ge2\sqrt{576}=48$, with equality when $t=\dfrac{576}{t}$, i.e. $t=24$.
Check: at $t=24$ the observations are $24,48,24,48$, mean $36$, variance $\dfrac{4\cdot144}{4}=144$.
originality_note: New: a data set depending on t whose variance reduces to an increasing function of s = t + 576/t, so AM-GM on s gives the least variance (way 2: a quantity of a moving family, then optimised). Closest known: AM-GM minimum of t + a/t. Different because: the quantity minimised is a variance, which must first be rewritten in terms of s.

key_step: Rewriting the variance as a function of s = t + 576/t and applying AM-GM.
justification: Two ideas linked (variance algebra, AM-GM) in numerical format with a simplification that must be exact. Comparable to two-stage L3 numericals; above 2026-P2-Q12 (L2).
